messages:
incident-bot: Paging: SLO breach on /v1/generate in us-west2. p99 crossed 7s, sustained for ~8m. Autopager -> #incidents.
Sam H: I'm on it. seeing p95 ~900ms, p99 7.2s. Streaming stalls in traces.
Marta L: Also seeing elevated connection queuing on router proxies in us-west2 (ebs-proxy-*-usw2).
Sam H: Adding traces. root cause looks like routing misassignments -> big fanout to a few hot shards.
Jeff C: Any recent router policy rollouts?
deploy-bot: deploy/user/router-policy v3.14.0 promoted to us-* at 2026-03-15T08:43:12Z by marta.l (canary 10% -> 100%).
Marta L: That matches timing. v3.14 introduced 'narrowing' rule to prefer local shard affinity in certain hash ranges.
Kai (oncall): Paging handoff to me in 5. I'm connecting to traces now.
Anya - SRE: I can run quick heatmap to confirm hot partition. giving query: `service:router AND region:us-west2 | group_by(shard) | count()`
Sam H: heatmap looks like shards 42/43/44 at 8-10x baseline. streaming session count jumped and KV cache misses increased.
Anya - SRE: Raw log snippet from router at 08:46:
```
[08:46:11] router: assign_request user_hash=0x1f4a shard=42 route=local_v3 policy=v3.14 dropped_to_queue=true
[08:46:12] router: forward_to_backend shard=42 backend=be-42-1 latency=512ms
[08:46:12] router: backend=be-42-1 queued=120 active_streams=0
```
Jeff C: backend=be-42-1 queued=120 active_streams=0 -> suggests misrouting lots of non-streaming traffic to streaming-optimized backends, causing stalls.
Marta L: v3.14 had a bug where non-streaming routes were matched by the 'prefer-local' predicate due to a prefix order change. That would concentrate general-gen traffic on streaming shards.
Kai (oncall): Confirmed in routing telemetry: route_tag 'local_v3' has +65% of cross-tenant traffic for key ranges (0x1f00-0x1fff).
Sam H: Customer impact? any 5xxs or request drops?
Anya - SRE: No 5xx surge, mostly increased latency and timeouts on streaming clients. CS reported a small set of accounts with degraded streaming sessions.
Jeff C: Action plan: 1) roll back router-policy to v3.13 in us-west2, 2) temporarily drain the hot backends, 3) increase ingress autoscale for short term.
Marta L: I'm preparing rollback. rolling back canary -> full revert command: `deployctl rollback router-policy --version v3.13 --region us-west2`
Kai (oncall): I'll start draining be-42-* group. Command: `routesvc drain --backend be-42 --grace 30s`
Sam H: Also flip fallback routing to global-rr for affected shards to spread load: `routerctl set-fallback shard=42 policy=global-rr`
Jeff C: Notify support/CS with current mitigation and ETA ~10-15m.
Sam H: @support Can you message affected customers with 'we're mitigating increased latency for streaming sessions in us-west2; temporary workaround may be required'?
Anya - SRE: Rollback started at 08:51:23Z. progress: canary 100% -> rollback initiated.
deploy-bot: rollback/router-policy v3.13 triggered by marta.l at 2026-03-15T08:51:23Z.
Marta L: Rollback complete at 08:53:05Z. Telemetry back to 3% of previous p99 peak for /v1/generate.
Kai (oncall): Drain complete for be-42 group. active queues dropped from 120 -> 6. Deployed `set-fallback` applied.
Anya - SRE: Post-rollback metrics: p95 400-700ms, p99 trending down to ~1.2s now. Streaming stall errors dropping.
Sam H: Running a follow-up check for misrouted keys: `select route, count(*) from routing_logs where region='us-west2' and timestamp > '2026-03-15T08:40' group by route` -> local_v3: 78k, global-rr: 12k pre-rollback.
Jeff C: Good. We should keep roll back in us-west2 and pause global rollout. Also schedule focused postmortem (owner: Jeff C).
Marta L: I'll open a rollback PR to pin policy to v3.13 until patch.
Kai (oncall): For live mitigation we should also add a temporary guard to avoid matching non-streaming flags in the 'prefer-local' predicate. I'll push a hotfix config: `predicate.exclude = has_flag(streaming)==false`
Sam H: Any customer-visible incidents opened?
Jeff C: Creating incident ticket now and tagging affected accounts. severity: S3 (partial degradation).
Anya - SRE: I'll keep monitoring for an hour and collect sample traces for scope. grabbing tracelogs -> attaching to ticket.
Marta L: Root cause hypothesis: policy change reordered predicate evaluation; unexpected prefix overlap caused general traffic to match streaming-local predicate -> hot partitioning of generic gen traffic -> tail latency spike.
Sam H: Postmortem actions to include: 1) tighten unit tests for routing predicate precedence, 2) add rollout guard for route skew (auto-pause if top-5 shards > 5x baseline), 3) improve streaming vs non-streaming route tagging.
deploy-bot: Note: rollback audit log stored: /deploys/router-policy/rollback/1761239998
Jeff C: Handing back to oncall. Kai, keep watch. I'll own postmortem and customer comms.
Kai (oncall): Acknowledged. I'll watch 08:55-09:55 window. ping @incident-bot if p99 > 2s again.
Sam H: Thanks all. Closing thread when p99 stable for 30m.
incident-bot: Note added to incident-ticket #INC-2026-0315-07: "Router policy rollout v3.14 caused local affinity misrouting; rollback to v3.13 mitigated tail latency."
Jeff C: Assigning postmortem owner -> Jeff C. ETA draft 48h.
Anya - SRE: Collected artifacts: heatmap, traces (session ids), router logs, deploy logs. Attaching to the ticket.
Marta L: I'll file a hotfix PR and link the test cases.
Sam H: Final check: p99 now 1.0s, p95 500ms. Looks good.
Kai (oncall): Keeping monitoring. If anything else spikes I'll reopen.
Jeff C: Thanks team. We'll run the postmortem and action items.
